{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RUNNxo1VtWvDSxLBbDs8XE","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/bin/sh\n# stage_test.sh — governed stage gate. Runs one slice of the authoritative suite.\n#\n# Same contract as full_test.sh, scoped to the cases a single story owns: build the decoder,\n# then run the installed toml-test suite over the pattern given as $1. Exit status is the\n# verdict and the whole verdict. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\nif [ $# -ne 1 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: stage_test.sh <toml-test -run pattern>\" >&2\n  exit 2\nfi\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run \"$1\"\n----\n#!/bin/sh\n# Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.\n#\n# Imported sources land in sources/ inside the application directory, so this is\n# normally invoked as `sh sources/run_conformance.sh` from that directory.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh                        # full suite\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run 'valid/string/*'  # one group\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -json                  # machine-readable\n#\n# Environment:\n#   DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and\n#              deliberately has no default implementation language.\n#   TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)\n#\n# Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md:\n# 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero\n# when it ran and the decoder failed. A precondition of the harness is never charged to the build.\n\nset -u\n\nif [ -z \"${DECODER:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: DECODER is not set; give the command that runs your decoder.\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST:-}\" ] && [ -x \"${TOML_TEST}\" ]; then\n    HARNESS=\"${TOML_TEST}\"\nelif command -v toml-test >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    HARNESS=\"$(command -v toml-test)\"\nelse\n    cat >&2 <<'EOF'\nerror: toml-test not found.\n\nInstall the harness once:\n\n    sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nor set TOML_TEST to an existing binary:\n\n    TOML_TEST=/path/to/toml-test sh sources/run_conformance.sh\nEOF\n    # 2, not the shell's own 127: an uninstalled harness says nothing about the decoder, and 127\n    # would be read as an ordinary nonzero exit and charged against the build as a product FAIL.\n    exit 2\nfi\n\n# The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, \"the authoritative suite passed\"\n# names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a\n# different version on a different machine is a different exam. Recorded always, and enforced\n# when the caller states which version it expects.\nHARNESS_VERSION=\"$(\"${HARNESS}\" version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)\"\necho \"harness: ${HARNESS} ${HARNESS_VERSION:-(version unknown)}\" >&2\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-}\" ] && [ -n \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" ]; then\n    case \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" in\n        *\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"*) ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"error: harness is ${HARNESS_VERSION}, expected ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}.\" >&2\n            echo \"Run: sh sources/setup_harness.sh\" >&2\n            exit 2\n            ;;\n    esac\nfi\n\nNO_COLOR=1 exec \"${HARNESS}\" test -toml 1.0 -decoder \"${DECODER}\" \"$@\"\n----\ntotal 16\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 14 08:55 .\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 14 08:56 ..\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  449 Oct 14 08:47 full_test.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 2707 Oct 14 08:47 run_conformance.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 1292 Oct 14 08:47 setup_harness.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 1268 Oct 14 08:47 stage_contract.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  641 Oct 14 08:47 stage_test.sh\n/home/barlo/.local/bin/toml-test","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5b988064-5a96-4ccf-9bfd-d1c57bd510ed","uuid":"4dd5f45d-9ae4-4186-a322-9b1b673e7afe","timestamp":"2026-10-14T12:56:51.816Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#!/bin/sh\n# stage_test.sh — governed stage gate. Recorded always, and enforced\n# when the caller states which version it expects.\nHARNESS_VERSION=\"$(\"${HARNESS}\" version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)\"\necho \"harness: ${HARNESS} ${HARNESS_VERSION:-(version unknown)}\" >&2\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-}\" ] && [ -n \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" ]; then\n    case \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" in\n        *\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"*) ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"error: harness is ${HARNESS_VERSION}, expected ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}.\" >&2\n            echo \"Run: sh sources/setup_harness.sh\" >&2\n            exit 2\n            ;;\n    esac\nfi\n\nNO_COLOR=1 exec \"${HARNESS}\" test -toml 1.0 -decoder \"${DECODER}\" \"$@\"\n----\ntotal 16\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 14 08:55 .\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 14 08:56 ..\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  449 Oct 14 08:47 full_test.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 2707 Oct 14 08:47 run_conformance.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 1292 Oct 14 08:47 setup_harness.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 1268 Oct 14 08:47 stage_contract.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  641 Oct 14 08:47 stage_test.sh\n/home/barlo/.local/bin/toml-test","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01RUNNxo1VtWvDSxLBbDs8XE","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017aQ8EEy3FTycX4BV2JpgbJ","type":"tool_result","content":"// Package toml decodes TOML v1.0.0 documents using only the standard library.\npackage toml\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"io\"\n)\n\n// ErrNotImplemented is returned by Decode until the parser is built.\nvar ErrNotImplemented = errors.New(\"toml: decoder not implemented\")\n\n// Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.\n// This foundational stub reads nothing and always reports ErrNotImplemented.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\treturn nil, ErrNotImplemented\n}\n----\npackage toml\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\nfunc TestDecodeStubReportsNotImplemented(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname  string\n\t\tinput string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"empty\", input: \"\"},\n\t\t{name: \"single key\", input: \"key = 1\\n\"},\n\t\t{name: \"table\", input: \"[table]\\nkey = \\\"v\\\"\\n\"},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tdoc, err := Decode(strings.NewReader(tt.input))\n\t\t\tif !errors.Is(err, ErrNotImplemented) {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Decode(%q) error = %v, want %v\", tt.input, err, ErrNotImplemented)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif doc != nil {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Decode(%q) = %v, want nil document\", tt.input, doc)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n----\n// Command toml-decoder reads a TOML document on stdin and writes its\n// tagged-JSON description to stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr and malformed\n// input exits non-zero.\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"os\"\n\n\t\"github.com/owner/toml-decoder/internal/toml\"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\tif err := run(os.Stdin, os.Stdout); err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, \"toml-decoder:\", err)\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n\n// run decodes the document on in and encodes the result as JSON to out.\nfunc run(in io.Reader, out io.Writer) error {\n\tdoc, err := toml.Decode(in)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"decode: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn json.NewEncoder(out).Encode(doc)\n}\n----\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"github.com/owner/toml-decoder/internal/toml\"\n)\n\nconst moduleRoot = \"../..\"\n\nfunc TestGoModDeclaresModuleWithoutRequire(t *testing.T) {\n\tdata, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(moduleRoot, \"go.mod\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"read go.mod: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\ttext := string(data)\n\tif strings.Contains(text, \"require\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"go.mod declares a require directive:\\n%s\", text)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(text, \"module github.com/owner/toml-decoder\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"go.mod does not declare the module path:\\n%s\", text)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestEntryPointIsPackageMain(t *testing.T) {\n\tdata, err := os.ReadFile(\"main.go\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"read main.go: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(string(data), \"package main\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"main.go is not a package main\")\n\t}\n\tinfo, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(moduleRoot, \"internal\", \"toml\"))\n\tif err != nil || !info.IsDir() {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"internal/toml is not a directory: %v\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestDecoderCommandBuildsWithStandardLibrary(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), \"toml-decoder\")\n\tcmd := exec.Command(\"go\", \"build\", \"-o\", bin, \"./cmd/toml-decoder\")\n\tcmd.Dir = moduleRoot\n\tif out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"go build failed: %v\\n%s\", err, out)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := os.Stat(bin); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"built binary missing: %v\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestRunReportsStubDecoderAsError(t *testing.T) {\n\tvar out bytes.Buffer\n\terr := run(strings.NewReader(\"key = 1\\n\"), &out)\n\tif !errors.Is(err, toml.ErrNotImplemented) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"run error = %v, want wrapping %v\", err, toml.ErrNotImplemented)\n\t}\n\tif out.Len() != 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"run wrote %q to stdout on failure, want nothing\", out.String())\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestBinaryExitsNonZeroWithEmptyStdout(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), \"toml-decoder\")\n\tbuild := exec.Command(\"go\", \"build\", \"-o\", bin, \"./cmd/toml-decoder\")\n\tbuild.Dir = moduleRoot\n\tif out, err := build.CombinedOutput(); {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Vs9Rtb3NShjsev6S4rwHM8","type":"tool_result","content":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.\n\ntoml-test v2.2.0 [/tmp/td-stub] [no encoder]\nskipped tests: 861\n  valid tests:   0 passed, 23 failed\nencoder tests: no encoder command given\ninvalid tests:   0 passed,  0 failed\nShell cwd was reset to /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5b988064-5a96-4ccf-9bfd-d1c57bd510ed","uuid":"fd517b93-9f31-4009-b8ab-e1b8694b7474","timestamp":"2026-10-14T12:57:10.649Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.\n\ntoml-test v2.2.0 [/tmp/td-stub] [no encoder]\nskipped tests: 861\n  valid tests:   0 passed, 23 failed\nencoder tests: no encoder command given\ninvalid tests:   0 passed,  0 failed","stderr":"\nShell cwd was reset to /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Vs9Rtb3NShjsev6S4rwHM8","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

They now use a bad escape. It just passes without testing anything.\n\n**Choices I made**\n\n- Dotted keys and table headers are rejected as syntax errors.
